title: Why Female Immunity Runs Hotter
hook: Women get autoimmune diseases like lupus far more often than men. Over 1,000 genetic switches behave differently in male and female immune cells — a stronger defense that can misfire.
key_points: More than 1,000 genetic switches act differently in male versus female immune cells.
Female immune systems appear genetically tuned for stronger inflammatory responses.
That tuning is a real advantage against infection.
The same setting may make dangerous immune misfires more likely.
It helps explain why autoimmune diseases such as lupus hit women much harder.
content_html: Autoimmune diseases are strikingly lopsided by sex: lupus, for instance, is diagnosed in women far more often than in men. New work reported by ScienceDaily suggests the reason is written into how immune cells read their own genes.
extra_html:
Researchers found that more than 1,000 genetic switches — the regulatory elements that decide which genes get turned up or down — behave differently in male and female immune cells. The pattern points one direction: female immune systems appear genetically tuned toward stronger inflammatory responses.

That is a double-edged setting. A harder-hitting immune response is a genuine advantage against infection, which is part of why it likely evolved. But the same aggressiveness raises the odds of a misfire, where the system attacks the body's own tissue. Framing autoimmunity as the cost of a well-armed defense, rather than a random malfunction, gives researchers a much more specific place to look for treatments.

related.title: The 'Foamy' Brain Cells Linked to Aggressive MS
related.hook: Why does multiple sclerosis race ahead in some people and stay quiet in others? Brain tissue from severe cases reveals fat-stuffed immune cells that may flip from repair mode to relentless damage.

related.title: ADHD Looks Different in Women — and Gets Missed for Decades
related.hook: Girls with ADHD look distracted rather than disruptive, so diagnosis often waits until adulthood. The cost isn't just lost years — one UK study found women with ADHD die nearly nine years earlier.

flashcards.prompt: What did researchers find differs between male and female immune cells?
flashcards.back_html: More than 1,000 genetic switches behave differently — leaving female immune systems tuned for stronger inflammatory responses.

flashcards.prompt: Why might a stronger inflammatory response also be a liability?

choices.text: The same aggressive response can misfire against the body's own tissue
It uses up the immune system's fixed lifetime supply of antibodies
It blocks vaccines from working at all

flashcards.explanation_html: A defense tuned to react hard is better at clearing infections but more prone to turning on the body — which is what autoimmune disease is.
